stories.headline: Toia backs himself among NRL's best centres after premiership triumph
stories.summary: After helping the Sydney Roosters to premiership glory with a standout defensive performance against Bradman Best, Robert Toia tells Isaac Issa he feels he's among the best centres in the NRL.
stories.body:
Robert Toia was reluctant to rank himself among the NRL's top three centres during Grand Final week.

After helping the Sydney Roosters to premiership glory with a standout defensive performance against Bradman Best, he was ready to acknowledge the belief he has in his own ability.

"Everyone has an opinion. But personally, yeah, I like to think I'm the best," Toia told ESPN in the victorious Roosters dressing room.

It was a glimpse of the confidence behind his performance, with Toia still coming to terms with the achievement unfolding around him.

"I'm so speechless," he said.

"I can't believe this is real. It's so surreal."

Toia had been unwilling to nominate his place among the competition's leading centres when asked by ESPN earlier in the week.

On Sunday night, his assignment against Best gave him the opportunity to demonstrate why he belongs in that conversation.

The Newcastle star presented a significant challenge on the game's biggest stage, but Toia embraced the responsibility of containing one of the Knights' most dangerous attacking weapons.

"I just knew how big of an occasion it was, and I just knew the boys wanted me to do a job," Toia said.

"Like you said, Bradman Best is one of the best centres, and I pride myself on being one of the top centres, so I just had to do my job."

His defensive performance provided substance behind that self-belief.

Against an opponent capable of changing a game with a single carry, Toia delivered an important contribution to the Roosters' premiership triumph.

His explanation centred on the responsibility he felt towards his teammates and the respect he held for his opposite number. He understood the challenge, backed himself to meet it and knew what the players alongside him needed.

While Toia was confident in his ability, he remained measured when asked whether the premiership marked the beginning of a long and successful career.

"Hopefully, God willing," he said.

"I'm just taking it day by day, year by year, I guess. I'm hoping my body pulls up sweet."

He was more emphatic about the Roosters' chances of challenging again.

With players departing the premiership-winning squad, next season will bring changes. Toia believes the confidence within the group can carry into its title defence.

"Yeah, I'm so confident," he said.

"There's obviously some boys leaving, but the belief in this group is so massive.

"No doubt that we have the mindset and we have the boys, so we go again."

For now, the next campaign can wait.

Toia has a premiership to celebrate - and a performance on the biggest stage to reinforce his place among the game's leading centres.

stories.headline: Braves have 'zero regrets' about pitching Chris Sale in relief
stories.summary: Braves manager Walt Weiss has "zero regrets" about Chris Sale pitching out of the bullpen in the prior round, even though it kept him from starting Game 2 of the NLDS.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss said he has "zero regrets" about pitching Chris Sale out of the bullpen in the prior round, even though it prevented him from starting Game 2 of the National League Division Series on Sunday night.

Sale was originally lined up to start Sunday at Dodger Stadium on the normal four days' rest, but the Braves used him for four batters in the late stages of a win-or-go-home Game 3 of the wild-card series against the Philadelphia Phillies on Thursday night. Because of that, Sale didn't start against the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 2 -- an important matchup given the Braves' 5-3 loss in Saturday's opener of the best-of-five series.

The Braves instead went with their third straight bullpen game, starting with lefty Ray Kerr. Sale will start Game 3 in Atlanta on Tuesday.

"At the end of the day, we want full-strength Chris Sale," Weiss said. "I know him at 80% is really good, but that's what it came down to. We've given him extra rest all year, and it's served him very well. It allowed him to do what he did the other night, I think.

"... Not sure you're getting the best version of him pitching [Sunday]. We're certain we will pitching Game 3."

Sale, 37, put together another Cy Young-caliber season in 2026, going 14-9 with a 2.16 ERA in 162 2/3 innings. His best start came against the Dodgers on Aug. 27, when he pitched a shutout and reached triple digits with his fastball. Sale made 25 of his 27 starts with five or more days off in between. It was part of the Braves' efforts to preserve him for a full season, but also to do what he did with their season on the line.

In the eyes of some rival executives, though, that appearance might have been unnecessary.

The Braves were leading by four with two outs in the eighth inning when Sale was summoned to face Bryce Harper. Given his usage all season, the move surprised many. That he came back out to pitch the entire ninth inning surprised even more. All told, Sale faced five batters and threw 21 pitches.

Sale's presence is even more crucial to a Braves team that has seen its starting rotation thin out for the playoffs.

Ronald Acuna Jr., the Braves' star right fielder, gave a brief pause and an awkward smile when asked in the interview room about Sale not starting Game 2.

"I don't know what I'm going to say about this because I can't control that," Acuna said. "I can control what I can control. So today we go out and try to win. I'm doing my best, my team, too, and we'll see what happens today."

Asked if Sale wanted to start Game 2, Weiss said: "Chris always wants to throw. Sometimes you have to take it out of their hands because he'd pitch every day if we asked him to. Yeah, we know our club very well. We know Chris Sale very well. That's a decision we made to pitch him in Game 3."

stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 4 inactives: Coker ruled out for Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists.

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 4 Buzz

Week 4 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 4

Biggest concerns heading into Week 4
Players in London

Chig Okonkwo, TE, Commanders (hamstring): He has been limited in practice this week but is active. Okonkwo has missed the past two games and, though it is encouraging to have him back, I would not risk getting him into your lineups right away. After all, he will likely be third in the target pecking order in a game started by a backup QB. There is some upside long term, though, with Daniels potentially nearing a return. Okonkwo is a stash for TE-needy teams.

Terry McLaurin, WR, Commanders (hamstring): Washington's top receiver was added to the injury report Friday and is indeed inactive for Sunday's game. Stefon Diggs was already a strong start as both the top slot option for the Commanders and man-coverage target. The Colts have allowed the most yards to slot receivers and play man at the third-highest rate in the NFL. With McLaurin sitting, Diggs gets an added boost in volume.

Players with early starts

ACTIVE

Lamar Jackson, QB, Ravens (back): Jackson scared away fantasy managers when he was limited in Wednesday's practice because of a back injury. He later returned to full practice and is active in Week 4. Never bench him in fantasy.

Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (hamstring): Flowers was questionable headed into the weekend but is indeed active for today's game. He has earned must-start status as the clear focal point of the Ravens' passing attack.

DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Buffalo's top receiver had been limited in practice and even wore a red noncontact jersey. That's the same thing that happened last week, and Moore ended up playing and getting 10 targets. He is active for Week 4. Also working in Moore's favor is that Patriots star CB Christian Gonzalez is out this week. Moore is Buffalo's top target when going against man defense, and New England uses that coverage at the second-highest NFL rate. He should be started in all leagues this week.

D'Andre Swift, RB, Bears (knee): Swift was added to the team's official injury report Thursday, but did not carry an injury designation heading into Sunday. He is active and fantasy managers can start him without worry.

Tyson Bagent, QB, Bears (concussion): Bagent is back at practice and reportedly took first-team reps this week. He is active and currently expected to start. Those who were planning on streaming Case Keenum in superflex leagues should pivot to Bagent. Luther Burden III is the only Bears pass catcher to start with confidence this week.

Nico Collins, WR, Texans (hamstring): Collins logged limited practices to start the week before getting in a full session Friday. He is active for Week 4 against the Cowboys -- a strong matchup for the receiver. Fantasy managers should get him in their starting lineup with confidence.

Puka Nacua, WR, Rams (hip): The star receiver has been limited at practice this week, but coach Sean McVay said he is "good to go" for Week 4. He is indeed active. Even if he ends up being on a snap count, this one is as simple as it can get in fantasy football: Nacua is playing for the Rams, so he needs to start in fantasy.

Drake Maye, QB, Patriots (shoulder): Yes, Maye was a full participant all week and is active for Week 4. However, he appeared on the team's official injury report for the first time all season. It's a situation worth monitoring, but until we see otherwise, it's fine to bench Maye in fantasy. Some options to start instead include Bryce Young, Tyler Shough, Kyler Murray and Jacoby Brissett.

Kenyon Sadiq, TE, Jets (back): The popular waiver-wire pickup has been limited at practice because of a back injury but is active for Week 4. With both Adonai Mitchell and Mason Taylor out, Sadiq is once again a high-upside option. He can be played over Colston Loveland, Mark Andrews and Tucker Kraft.

Bucky Irving, RB, Buccaneers (glute): Irving was limited to start the week but is active for Week 4. He is the lone Tampa Bay player whom fantasy managers can trust with any confidence today. Not only has Irving seen 15-plus carries in each of the past two games, but he has been featured in the team's passing game as well. Additionally, the Packers have allowed the third-most RB rushing yards per game this season and have specifically allowed the most on outside runs. Irving ranks fourth in the NFL in rush yards on runs outside the tackles.

Tyjae Spears, RB, Titans (ankle): Spears is active and will play in Week 4. Though he saw the field on nearly half of all snaps in Week 3, the bulk of opportunities (21-3) went to Tony Pollard. Pollard missed practice Wednesday but returned to full practice after indicating it was just a "veteran rest day." Pollard is a low-floor flex option with volume upside. Spears is purely for desperate fantasy managers in deep leagues.

INACTIVE

Lane Johnson, OT, Eagles (personal): We don't typically mention when an offensive lineman is inactive, but this late-breaking news at least warrants a look. With Johnson out there is more volatility to the Eagles offense, especially the rushing attack. The good news for Philly is that the Rams will be without Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald this week. Both Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley, who has yet to score double-digit fantasy points in any game this season, have their fantasy floors lowered in this one. Still, fantasy managers have to start them. Just understand that there is now a bit more risk.

Players with late starts

ACTIVE

Keaton Mitchell, RB, Chargers (foot): Mitchell logged limited practices to start the week before elevating to full Friday. He is active for Week 4. Though he is not someone who fantasy managers should start this week against the Seahawks, his availability impacts Omarion Hampton. Last week, Mitchell and Kimani Vidal had more routes and targets than Hampton.

Ladd McConkey, WR, Chargers (foot): McConkey is active for Week 4. However, fantasy managers should seek to avoid McConkey (and all of the struggling Chargers offense) if possible against Seattle. The Seahawks have allowed the fewest yards and just two touchdowns to wideouts. They've also allowed only one deep pass, so you cannot even rely on a big play salvaging the day for you.

Mike Evans, WR, 49ers (ribs): Evans did not practice to start the week before participating Friday. He was a game-time decision, but is active Week 4. He will likely see a lot of Pat Surtain II. That makes him a "boom-or-bust" WR2 with some injury risk. Evans being active takes a lot of the shine away from those who thought about streaming Deebo Samuel Sr. this week.

Ruled out before Sunday Night Football
Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (quad): Coker is out for Week 4. It seemed likely after the Panthers elevated WR Ja'seem Reed from the practice squad on Saturday, so hopefully fantasy managers went in another direction. Panthers WR Brycen Tremayne is a pivot option for those who rolled the dice on Coker. He caught four out of six targets for 83 yards after Coker left early last week. He is a deep league flex-option against the Lions secondary that has allowed the fourth-most WR fantasy PPG.
Ruled out before Sunday
Jaycee Horn/Mike Jackson, CB, Panthers (quad/groin): Both of the Panthers' starting CBs were placed on IR this week. Both are expected to miss more than the minimum four required games. Carolina just became a much more fantasy-friendly matchup for receivers. It has made me change my mind on Detroit's Jameson Williams this week. I won't be sitting him.

Jayden Reed, WR, Packers (neck): Reed will undergo neck surgery and is out for the season.

Keenan Allen, WR, Colts (groin): Allen originally appeared on the injury report as "having a rest day," but that was later changed to add an injury. The Week 4 sleeper is out against the Commanders. That should mean even more volume for both Josh Downs and Tyler Warren, both of which should be started in a strong matchup. Washington is top two in touchdowns allowed to both receivers and tight ends entering Week 4.

Terrance Ferguson, TE, Rams (ankle): The tight end has been placed on IR and will miss four weeks. Ferguson has been really effective thus far, so he is worth stashing if you have an IR spot. Some tight ends to start in his place this week are Darren Waller, Juwan Johnson, Kenyon Sadiq and Dalton Schultz.

De'Von Achane, RB, Dolphins (knee): Miami's star back suffered a torn ACL and is out for the season. Ollie Gordon II and Jaylen Wright -- who has been a full participant in practice after missing Week 3 (stinger/foot) -- will be used now. Both were picked up in many fantasy leagues this week, but fantasy managers should take a wait-and-see approach. Not only are we uncertain as to how the work will be distributed, but the Dolphins also play the Vikings, who have allowed the fourth-fewest RB rushing yards (and no TDs) this season.

Justin Jefferson, WR, Vikings (ankle): One of the best receivers in the NFL has been ruled out for Week 4. That news pushes Jordan Addison into the high-end WR2 range. Go with Addison over McConkey, Malik Nabers, Jaylen Waddle and Emeka Egbuka. Consider Minnesota's Jauan Jennings to be a flex option, particularly for those in deeper leagues.

Breece Hall, RB, Jets (quad): Hall is "week-to-week" after leaving Week 3 early. He will not play in Week 4. Braelon Allen handled all the work after Hall exited and is in play this week as an RB2/flex option. The Bears have allowed 4.8 RB yards per carry, fourth highest in the NFL. Go with Allen over Hampton, Price, Rhamondre Stevenson and J.K. Dobbins. Isaiah Davis could handle passing downs. He is worth rostering, but should not be in starting lineups.

Travis Etienne Jr., RB, Saints (hamstring): The Saints' big free agent acquisition has been placed on IR and will miss at least four games. That leaves Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller as the team's new RB tandem. Kamara had been used over Miller in Week 3 and should be viewed as the top fantasy option here. I would expect the ground work to be split between the two, and all the passing-game volume should go to Kamara. Still, until we see an uptick in efficiency, Kamara is merely a flex option. This week, I would sit both Saints backs, as the Falcons have allowed minus-13 yards before contact this season.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring): He has not practiced this week and is out for Week 4. It's a big blow to fantasy managers and an Eagles passing attack that is also without Dallas Goedert. That would leave Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon as the team's top receivers. Of the two, I prefer Wicks -- but both are merely flex options. Stick with Wicks over Rome Odunze, Brian Thomas Jr., Marvin Harrison Jr and Quentin Johnston.

Jadarian Price, RB, Seahawks (chest): Price has been placed on IR and will miss at least four games. That leaves Emanuel Wilson and George Holani as the lead backs -- albeit in a tough matchup this week -- and in the flex range. Wilson is the preferred option, as we have already seen him handle a large workload and be productive this season. We do not know for sure how the workload will be distributed. Though the Chargers haven't done much well this season, they have been effective against the run.

Note: Seattle has designated Zach Charbonnet to return, which means the Seahawks have 21 days to activate Charbonnet. We don't know when exactly he will return, but this means he is getting closer. It's worth checking the waiver wire for him, especially with Price now on IR.

Baker Mayfield, QB, Buccaneers (thumb): Mayfield dislocated his thumb in Week 3 and will miss at least three weeks. That leaves undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels as the starter. He has rushing ability, gaining over 400 yards in three separate college seasons while adding 23 rushing scores during his college career. Still, he's only an option for those dealing with injuries in two-QB leagues. Given all the uncertainty, I would look to avoid all Tampa Bay pass catchers (including Egbuka) if possible. Irving is the only Tampa Bay player I would want to start in Week 4.

Jalen McMillan, WR, Buccaneers (knee): Oh, and McMillan has been placed on IR, meaning he will miss at least the next four games. It's the latest in what has been a litany of injuries that have forced the young receiver to miss time. With him out, expect Ted Hurst III to get more run. However, as outlined above, it's tough to trust any Tampa Bay receivers in fantasy while Mayfield is sidelined.

Jayden Daniels, QB, Commanders (elbow): Daniels has been ruled out for Week 4. He participated in practice this week -- albeit in a limited capacity -- which is encouraging for his future availability. The fact that he flew to London is also an encouraging sign. With him out, Marcus Mariota is in play as a strong streaming option. Indianapolis allows the third-most passing yards per game and generates pressure at the fourth-lowest rate. Play Mariota over Drake Maye, Justin Herbert, Bo Nix and Sam Darnold.

Rachaad White, RB, Commanders (shoulder): White has been a DNP at practice and has been ruled out for Week 4. The newly signed Austin Ekeler traveled overseas with the team and could be used in obvious passing-down situations. With the shaky backup situation here, Jacory Croskey-Merritt looks like an RB2 in a good matchup against the Colts, who have allowed the most RB rushing yards before contact. They also have allowed the second-most RB rushing touchdowns. JCM can be played over Omarion Hampton and all the popular waiver-wire RBs from this week.

stories.headline: AFL: Heavyweight trades loom large over AFL free agency period
stories.summary: Essendon and Hawthorn's jostling over Zach Merrett and deals for free agents Zak Butters and Ben King will headline another bumper trade and free agency period.
stories.body:
Essendon and Hawthorn's jostling over Zach Merrett and deals for free agents Zak Butters and Ben King will headline another bumper AFL trade and free agency period.

Brisbane's dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and GWS captain Toby Greene respectively strolled to Collingwood and Geelong after free agency opened on Friday, courtesy of their unrestricted status.

Port Adelaide superstar Butters and Gold Coast key forward King face a longer wait as restricted free agents.

The Power can match any bid for 26-year-old Butters, who nominated the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination over Geelong, and will want more than the first-round compensation they would otherwise garner.

As league-wide haggling ramps up when the trade period opens on Monday, the Bulldogs may well have to get creative at the negotiating table to satisfy Port.

Gold Coast have similarly canvassed matching a rival bid for King when Hawthorn officially come knocking for the Victorian spearhead.

A bid on Butters or King would generate band one compensation, currently valued at pick five for Port and pick seven for Gold Coast.

Complicating matters, Hawthorn is making another dash at Merrett after Essendon sensationally rejected offers for the gun midfielder in 2025.

The Hawks hold a respectable draft hand, with four draft picks between 15 and 33 on top of future first-round selections in 2027 and 2028.

Merrett, who turned 31 on Saturday, is entering the final year of his Bombers contract and clinched a seventh club best and fairest award after a disastrous two-win season.

With Butters and Merrett spurning Geelong's advances, the Cats have shifted their focus to injury-plagued Essendon defender Jordan Ridley, contracted until 2029, and St Kilda ruckman Rowan Marshall.

St Kilda asked for a player in exchange for Marshall after the contracted 30-year-old requested a trade away to the Cattery for a second straight season.

The Cats were not keen to entertain giving up young half-back Lawson Humphries but talks for Marshall remain ongoing.

In other wheelings and dealings, Gold Coast is expected to trade a late pick for Collingwood veteran Scott Pendlebury if King walks as a restricted free agent so as not to dilute their compensation pick.

Dumped GWS forward and 2024 Coleman medallist Jesse Hogan is also expected to join Collingwood for a late pick rather than waiting for delisted free agency.

Carlton are reportedly trying to prise contracted half-back Lachie Whitfield out of GWS, while trade speculation surrounds Nick Blakey after he and four other Sydney Swans players were banned on the eve of the finals.

Brisbane premiership winger Sam Marshall is eyeing a trade to St Kilda, Luke Pedlar wants a rare switch from Adelaide to Port Adelaide, and Geelong midfielder Jack Bowes is trying to get to Essendon.

Jack Viney, Melbourne's 2021 premiership vice-captain, on Thursday said a deal would be done after he met with West Coast.

Demons coach Steven King told the 32-year-old midfielder he was likely to be on the outer next season despite having two years remaining on his contract.

The free agency period ends on Friday, while the trade window wraps up on October 14.

stories.headline: Who most deserves the Ballon d'Or? Whittling down the 30-man short list
stories.summary: Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane are the three favorites to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or, but who actually deserves to win it?
stories.body:
For most of the past 15 years, there was really no point in campaigning for the men's Ballon d'Or -- it was going to the more obnoxiously successful of two men, Lionel Messi (eight-time winner) or Cristiano Ronaldo (five). Their personal -- and sometimes club -- rivalry defined the sport, to the point where even a rising star like Kylian Mbappé openly admitted he wasn't as good as them.

"It's not only me who knows that," he told writer Simon Kuper in "The Barcelona Complex." "Everyone knows it. If you tell yourself that you'll do better than them, it's beyond ego or determination -- it's lack of awareness. Those players are incomparable. They have broken all laws of statistics."

"I can't top them" probably isn't the healthiest thing in the world for a megastar to tell himself, but with Messi and Ronaldo finally having aged out of the competition -- Ronaldo hasn't finished in the top three of the voting in the 2020s, and Messi's final win came in 2023 -- now's the time to pounce.

Mbappé wants it. Lamine Yamal has said he wants it. Harry Kane thinks winning it would be "amazing." They're the three betting favorites for the award -- Kane's and Yamal's odds are both at +100 after a recent rise from Yamal, while Mbappé is at a longer +1000 -- but who actually deserves it?

After some late PR campaigns from players and clubs, voting for the award closed on Monday. It will go to the player who achieved the most between the beginning of the 2025-26 club season and the end of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Thirty players were officially nominated, but based on who has won the award in the past, we can narrow the field pretty quickly.

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how City recover from extraordinary guilty verdict

- Lindop: Liverpool can't afford to be without Isak, Gakpo in October

Eliminate anyone who played for Real Madrid last season

Eliminated: Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior

I'm sorry, but we have to start here. The three players above are all dynamite, and two have come pretty close to winning the award already -- Mbappé was 192 points behind Messi in 2023, and Vinícius was only 41 points behind Rodri in 2024.

Mbappé is indeed No. 3 in the betting odds, and his scorpionlike quick strike capabilities might make him the most terrifying player in the world. At any point, it feels as if you could be about eight seconds from a Mbappé goal. He's great.

He has also been part of a terribly disappointing club team for two straight years. Since Mbappé joined Real Madrid, the only trophies they've won were the UEFA Super Cup and the FIFA Intercontinental Cup in 2024, trophies tied to accomplishments of the team before his arrival.

Real Madrid have finished behind Barcelona in both of Mbappé's seasons, and after winning the UEFA Champions League in the season before his arrival, they haven't made it past the quarterfinals with him. The Ballon d'Or isn't for club underachievers.

Mbappé is a delicious goal scorer, but his inability to even pretend to contribute in defense has held the team back significantly, especially combined with Vinícius' own refusal to do so. Mbappé did, however, have a fantastic World Cup, which is why he's No. 3 on the list -- he won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and became the competition's all-time leading scorer. But even there, his team lost to Yamal's Spain and Kane's England.

It would feel awfully strange if Mbappé retired without a Ballon d'Or, but he didn't earn it in 2025-26, nor did anyone else on a trophy-less Real Madrid team.

That cuts the list to 27 guys.

Actually, eliminate anyone who didn't win a trophy

Eliminated: Bruno Fernandes, Sadio Mané, Julián Quiñones

Technically, players have taken the Ballon d'Or after a trophy-less campaign, but it's rare. Kevin Keegan did it in 1978, back when it was called the "France Football European Footballer of the Year"; Figo did it in 2000 after leading Portugal to the Euro 2000 semis (and making a seismic move from Barcelona to Real Madrid that summer); and Ronaldo did it after scoring 55 goals in 2013. That's it. That's the list.

We watched Mané win a trophy back in the winter, when Senegal upset Morocco in a contentious Africa Cup of Nations final, but they were stripped of the award in March, so it was technically a trophy-free campaign for him. And though Quiñones scored four goals for Mexico at the World Cup (and 33 for Al Qadsiah in the Saudi Pro League) and Fernandes set a Premier League assists record, the bar for accomplishments in a World Cup year is too high. You need a trophy.

Now we're down to 24.

If you won only one trophy, you had better be an attacker

Eliminated: Marc Cucurella, Gabriel Magalhães, Declan Rice, William Saliba

Sorry, I don't make the rules. (I mean, I am kind of making the rules here, but they're based on history.) The one-trophy guys tend to be goal scorers -- Messi in 2019, the original Ronaldo in 2002, Roberto Baggio in 1993, Jean-Pierre Papin in 1990, Ruud Gullit in 1987, Michel Platini in 1983, Karl-Heinz Rumenigge in 1981, Keegan in 1979.

Arsenal won the Premier League with a fantastic core of midfielders such as Rice and defenders such as Gabriel and Saliba, and Cucurella, a fullback, was nearly error-free during Spain's World Cup run. But none of these guys score much.

That gets them eliminated, and it gets us down to 20 contenders.

When in doubt, eliminate anyone who had a disappointing World Cup (or didn't play in it)

Eliminated: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, João Neves, Willian Pacho, Vitinha

In a World Cup year, the Ballon d'Or becomes extremely World Cup-centric. It's why Mbappé still has a prayer this year, and it's a main reason why Messi won in 2023 (after Argentina won 2022's winter World Cup), why Luka Modric won in 2018 (after Croatia's run to the final), why Manuel Neuer finished third in 2014 (after Germany's win), why Andres Iniesta and Xavi Hernandez finished second and third in 2010 (after Spain's win), why Fabio Cannavaro won in 2006 (after Italy's win), and on and on.

Unfortunately for a number of Paris Saint-Germain stars, a lack of World Cup success gets them eliminated. World Cup expansion means Georgia's Kvaratskhelia might have hope of playing there one day, but he didn't this summer, while Marquinhos was part of a disappointing Brazilian squad, Pacho's Ecuador bowed out in the round of 32, and Mendes, Neves and Vitinha were all part of a Portugal team that was supposed to contend and didn't. (I guess you could say that Ronaldo got four of his Portuguese teammates eliminated from this competition, too.)

This knocks our list all the way down to 14 remaining players.

You have to be the best player on your club team (or have a case that you are)

Eliminated: Luis Díaz, Pau Cubarsí, Fabián Ruiz, Ferran Torres, Dayot Upamecano

It seems fair, right? Cubarsí is a ridiculously sound center back, especially for a 19-year-old, and Upamecano is a major key to Bayern Munich's high-wire attacking style. Díaz proved his incredible "glue guy" characteristics when he left Liverpool for Bayern and the former fell apart, while the latter achieved a new level of attacking prowess. But few would make the case that these guys are better than Barça's Yamal or Raphinha, or Bayern's Kane or Michael Olise.

Torres, meanwhile, scored the World Cup-winning goal, but Barça let him leave for PSG. So, let's cross these five off our list. Now we're down to nine.

You should be among the top 3 in your position

Eliminated: Ousmane Dembélé, Lautaro Martínez, Lionel Messi

The final nine are all extremely accomplished and talented, so we have to raise the bar even higher. Using the summer's FC 100 voting, we can eliminate Martínez (No. 6 center forward), Messi (No. 5 wide forward) and Dembélé (No. 4 center forward). All three had excellent seasons and/or World Cup campaigns, but others have just been a little bit better in 2025-26. That gets us down to six.

Has anyone in your position ever won the Ballon d'Or?

Eliminated: Achraf Hakimi

Sometimes a non-attacker can transcend the counting stats and win the award. Rodri did, after all, in 2024 following the success of both Spain and Manchester City, and Modric won in 2018 after combining major club success (Real Madrid) with a World Cup run (Croatia). Cannavaro was among the best defenders of the 2000s and rode a World Cup title to victory over Italian teammate Gianluigi Buffon (also not a forward, obviously) in 2006. But no fullback has yet taken the award.

That's apparently a bridge too far. The closest thing was when a sweeper such as Matthias Sammer (1996) or Franz Beckenbauer (1972 and 1976) did the deed, but sweepers still aren't fullbacks, and that was three and five decades ago. Hakimi is the best fullback in the world and has been for a while, but he's not getting the nod.

We're down to five.

How was your club season?

Eliminated: Rodri

Watching Rodri in person at the World Cup was an incredible experience. He saw every potential counterattack against Spain developing 10 seconds in advance and was always in place to intercept the ball before it could start moving in the other direction. He was a timepiece, always keeping Spain from moving too slowly or too quickly. He probably benefited a bit from the slower pace of international play, but he was note-perfect during the tournament and deserved the Golden Ball award.

However, that all came on the heels of a club season in which he started only 17 league games for Manchester City while still trying to return to full form after his 2024 knee injury. The only reason he's on the list is because of the World Cup, and the four remaining guys on this list combined club success with great World Cup performances.

Your finalists

This process of elimination has left us with four potential winners, listed alphabetically:

Erling Haaland, 26, Manchester City/Norway

Relevant stats (club and country): 64 matches (2.19 PPG), 5,146 minutes, 58 goals, 11 assists from 45 chances created, World Cup quarterfinal, two trophies (FA Cup, Carabao Cup)

Harry Kane, 33, Bayern Munich/England

Relevant stats: 65 matches (2.60 PPG), 5,220 minutes, 73 goals, eight assists from 80 chances created, World Cup third place, three trophies (Bundesliga, German Cup, German Supercup)

Michael Olise, 24, Bayern Munich/France

Relevant stats: 69 matches (2.54 PPG), 5,314 minutes, 27 goals, 34 assists from 170 chances created, World Cup fourth place, three trophies (Bundesliga, German Cup, German Supercup)

Lamine Yamal, 19, Barcelona/Spain

Relevant stats: 57 matches (2.46 PPG), 4,574 minutes, 25 goals, 20 assists from 131 chances created, World Cup champion, three trophies (World Cup, LaLiga, Spanish Supercopa)

Actually, listing each player's relevant stats gives me an opportunity to address one of this year's primary Ballon d'Or controversies: the non-inclusion of Raphinha, Yamal's Barça teammate -- and maybe the hottest player in the world right now -- on the 30-man short list. Thirty players is a lot, and Raphinha had an obvious case, but in the time frame around which the award is based, he played only 40 matches and scored 21 goals with eight assists. He battled injuries and form, he barely played for Brazil at the World Cup (130 minutes, zero goals and assists), and he didn't really catch fire until the time frame ended. Consider him an early front-runner for 2027 (though I've already made my prediction in that race).

The betting odds tell us that two of these four players are far more likely to win than the other two, but all four have solid cases.

The case for Haaland

Haaland enjoyed another strong club season, scoring 38 goals with nine assists in all competitions. That almost sounds underwhelming by his standards, but it is still fantastic for someone in the best league in the club universe. Haaland might have enjoyed himself more than anyone else at the World Cup. His seven goals were the most by a World Cup debutant since 1974 (Poland's Grzegorz Lato), and he led Norway to its best-ever finish, a quarterfinal run that included a win over Brazil. (Naturally, he scored both of Norway's goals in that match.)

Haaland was also a bit of a pop culture phenomenon, buying cowboy hats, eating pastrami sandwiches and basically winning over every casual American sports fan. The World Cup belonged to him as much as anyone, and that usually earns you lots of Ballon d'Or votes. His case is likely dinged by both Manchester City's second-place finish to Arsenal in the Premier League and the dark clouds of the City scandal (which had nothing to do with him). But I was very surprised to see his odds for the award at only +4000, tied for eighth with Cubarsí, Dembélé, Olise and Bellingham. He'd be in my top five at worst.

The case for Olise

For my money, Olise is the best player in the world at the moment. That doesn't automatically mean he should win, and it's partially because of how he has started this new season. He already has eight goals and three assists in seven matches for Bayern, and when France needed a spark against Belgium this week in the UEFA Nations League, guess who sprang off the bench and immediately made the difference? But I was already starting to believe in his superiority last season.

Olise scored 22 goals with 26 assists in all competitions -- six to Kane -- for Bayern in 2025-26, a season in which he established himself as the best creator in the world. His touch and vision are sublime, and when it's time for him to do it himself, he's more than OK with doing that.

As with Haaland, Olise's odds are +4000, which is to say he's obviously not going to win it. But he'd be in my top three. He led the World Cup in assists with seven (no one else had more than four), and really, only a finishing slump held him back: He attempted 20 shots worth 2.5 xG, but none went in the net. But that's fine. For those of us in the Olise Is the Best in the World club, he can remain our little secret for a little while longer.

The case for Yamal

This is an award for 2025-26, but the case for Yamal almost has to start with Spain's current 40-match (and more than four-year) unbeaten streak. It correlates almost perfectly with the emergence of Yamal. He played 18 minutes in Spain's last defeat -- a 1-0 friendly loss to Colombia in March 2024 and his fifth appearance for Spain as a 16-year-old -- but during this unbeaten streak, he has started 28 of 40 matches. In this span, he's fourth on the team in minutes (2,305), third in goals (eight), second in shots on goal (36), progressive carries (320) and completed crosses (24) and first in assists (12), chances created (55), line-breaking passes received (297), ground duels won (184) and fouls suffered (44). Hell, he is also second in successful tackles (52) and third in ball recoveries (117).

Yamal wasn't even at full strength during the World Cup, having rushed back from injury, but he still played 615 of 750 minutes, and his mere presence out wide stretched and stressed defenses in ways that opened up opportunities for others. He was content playing more of a supporting role, refused to force the issue and lifted his second major international trophy before his 20th birthday.

Yamal has been the most valuable player on both the most successful international team of the 2020s and the team that has won the last two LaLiga crowns. And his magnetic personality, which comes through in virtually any interview, certainly doesn't hurt his Ballon d'Or cause. Putting together a career that rivals Messi's or Ronaldo's will take a level of longevity that we don't yet know he has, but at worst he's the second-most successful teenager ever behind Pele (who not only won a World Cup but also had two 50-goal campaigns).

The case for Kane

I'm finishing this list with Kane because, honestly, his is the easiest case to make. Yamal seems to be picking up momentum in the race, at least if betting odds are to be believed (and they frequently are), and if he wins it will be hard to say it was unjust. But look again at the stats above. Kane played eight more matches and over 600 more minutes than Yamal -- which is to say, he stayed healthier than a player 14 years his junior -- and he produced 81 combined goals and assists, a full 36 more than Yamal.

Does he play for one of the two most talented and prolific attacks in the world? Obviously. But so does Yamal!

Kane is England's all-time leading goal scorer and has the second-most goals in the history of the Premier League, but he achieved a new level of prowess in his 16th professional season. He scored over 60 club goals in all competitions for the first time, then he scored six goals in seven matches while leading England to the World Cup semifinals for the second time.

You could easily say that, when you're in doubt regarding whom to vote for, you should choose the older player who might not get another chance. But you don't even need to use that as a tiebreaker for Kane against Yamal because I don't think it's tied. He won nearly as much as Yamal at the World Cup, won every domestic trophy with Bayern and posted far superior statistics.

If I had a guess, I'd say Yamal wins at this point because of the late PR push. If I had a vote, however, I'd go with Kane.

stories.headline: USMNT's young stars shine to give Pochettino 'fantastic problem'
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said that the number of players performing at a high level is "a fantastic problem to have" after teenagers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall propelled the USMNT to 3-0 win over rivals Mexico on Saturday.
stories.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said that the number of players performing at a high level is "a fantastic problem to have" after teenagers Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall propelled the USMNT to 3-0 win over rivals Mexico on Saturday.

The U.S. endured a difficult first half, and scored completely against the run of play in the 28th minute when Hall converted from close range after Mexico keeper Raúl Rangel spilled Gio Reyna's low cross right in front of goal.

- Cavan Sullivan has arrived: U.S. phenom's goal caps a memorable win over Mexico

- Márquez bemoans 'terrible mistakes' as Mexico humbled by USMNT

- USMNT player ratings: Sullivan, Hall 9/10 in big win vs. Mexico

The USMNT began to make more headway in the second half, and doubled its lead in the 62nd minute when Sullivan intercepted a pass from Rangel, and chipped the ball into the net from 35 yards out. The match lost its edge when Mexico's Mateo Chávez was red carded in the 67th minute following a scrap with Sebastian Berhalter.

Malik Tillman finished off the scoring in the 84th minute, latching onto another wayward Mexico pass to firing into the net.

Hall, 18, is just the third USMNT player to score in his first three national team appearances, while 17-year-old Sullivan became the youngest scorer in USMNT history.

"I think it's a fantastic problem for us," Pochettino said about the performances of his team's young players. "I think we will take the right decision in the right moment, but I think it's a very good problem to see.

"Now it's not a moment at all, but yes, we appreciate that situation and of course hope that we will be in that situation that young players perform in the way that they deserve to be with us."

Pochettino also pronounced himself pleased with the way his side weathered Mexico's early pressure.

"I think that this, overall, was a great opportunity to discover ourself, to see ourselves in a difficult game with a very good team. Again, Mexico is a great team," Pochettino said.

"Yes, I think two different maybe halves. The first half I think Mexico started really well. They forced us to play back. We never connected. We were losing all the duels. And then we start to grow after 15, 20 minutes. And I think it was a good lesson the first half because it was the sense of work all together, suffer together even when you are not playing well in the way that you plan to play."

But Pochettino couldn't help but admire the performance of Sullivan, who impressed with his work on both sides the ball.

"I think he's a talented player with enormous quality, but with a very good balance, in possession and out of possession," Pochettino said about Sullivan. "He's a fighter, he's a warrior. It's difficult to find this type of player with a tremendous quality.

"And then I think Cavan showed in possession with the ball on the field [and] when he need to be chasing people and recover the ball. That is my impression after maybe three weeks together. And that is unbelievable, to have a player like this. I think it's a fantastic news for USA. Hope that continues in that way."

Pochettino was careful to laud Sullivan's young teammates as well, who have largely impressed during this window.

"It's a big moment because we need to be right with them," Pochettino said about the win, and the path forward. "We need to protect them. We need to support them. Our responsibility now is that this group of talented players grow in the right direction."

stories.headline: LeBron James calls scrimmage 'great first step' for new-look 76ers
stories.summary: Throngs of fans waited in lines more than 10-deep to watch LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and the rest of the 76ers take part in Saturday's scrimmage.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- It might have been the basketball equivalent of a dress rehearsal, but the 76ers' intrasquad scrimmage Saturday certainly gave a promising glimpse of what could be in store when the curtain actually comes up for the 2026-27 NBA season.

Philadelphia hosted its annual Blue-White game in front of approximately 10,000 fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena, moving the exhibition from their G League affiliate's home in Delaware to accommodate the added interest in the new-look team.

While throngs of fans waited in lines more than 10-deep in the atrium an hour before the noon start, there was plenty of on-court action from LeBron James, Jaylen Brown & Co. to enjoy as soon as the scrimmage started.

"To be able to take what we've done on the practice floor, bring it to a game floor situation around our fans ... it was a great first step in the direction we're trying to go," James said.

Longtime Sixers public address announcer Matt Cord, who had retired before deciding to come back once Philadelphia had its historic summer, announced the starters for the Blue team.

First Tyrese Maxey, then VJ Edgecombe, then Brown, then James and then the man in the middle who has been with the franchise for 13 years.

"7-2 from Cameroon, No. 21, Joel 'The Processsss' Embiiddddd!" Cord bellowed.

"It doesn't matter who gets announced first, last, second, third," Embiid said.

But the cheers that followed every name did mean something to him.

"We love the fans," Embiid said. "We want them, and we need them to be part of this. I mentioned it at media day: It's already hard enough to win as a group that gets together for the first year. So we're going to need all we can, whether it's from everybody in this building, the fans, the outside people, we're going to need to get together. We're going to need all the support possible."

The Sixers didn't keep an official box score, but the stats mattered far less than some of the sequences that showed the early chemistry that is developing after a week of training camp, including James finding a trailing Embiid for an above-the-break 3.

"Guys are going to use their speed against people and try to score a quick basket, and if we don't have anything, I'm the trail guy," Embiid said matter-of-factly.

Both Maxey and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope delivered feeds to James for alley-oop dunks that the 41-year-old star finished with ease. Embiid got his 7-foot frame to lift high enough to both block springy second-year guard Edgecombe and have a dunk of his own.

"Pretty good, not bad," a noticeably slimmed-down Embiid said when asked how he felt physically compared to last season. Then he showed his sense of humor is as strong as ever.

"That's probably the last dunk of my career," Embiid said with a smirk.

While James has had only four official Sixers practices, plus the scrimmage, it was enough for him to conclude that Embiid is a different player than the guy he won a gold medal with at the Paris Olympics two summers ago.

"The difference between '24 and now, he's just so much more healthier," James said. "He hasn't missed a practice. He's been in damn near everything that we've done. Pretty much. They've had to sit him out at times, even when he wanted to keep going. ... So it's been good. Actually, great."

Philadelphia limited the scrimmage to three 10-minute quarters but started each period with the scoreboard set to 80-80 to simulate an end-of-game scenario.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse, who thanked the crowd for its support after the scrimmage, is giving the team the day off Sunday before it opens its four-game preseason slate by hosting the New York Knicks on Monday.

"It will be good to get out there with some of our guys to just get a rhythm," James said of the preseason schedule. "At the same time, also not overdo it, because we're putting a lot into our practices right now, fine-tuning what we want to do once the [regular-season] games come, but there'll be opportunities when we get out there in the preseason."

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: A fairytale Knights run ends in a Newcastle nightmare
stories.summary: The Sydney Roosters' 19-18 victory delivered the premiership farewell Daly Cherry-Evans had chased, while leaving the Knights one point short of completing their fairytale run.
stories.body:
For a moment, Kalyn Ponga made Newcastle believe the fairytale had one more chapter.

A loose Roosters tap-back, a burst into open space and a sprint almost the length of the field. Suddenly, the Knights led 12-0 and a city that had waited 25 years for another grand final could begin to imagine the ultimate reward.

Instead, Newcastle were left to contemplate how close they had come.

The Sydney Roosters' 19-18 victory delivered the premiership farewell Daly Cherry-Evans had chased, while leaving the Knights one point short of completing their remarkable transformation.

Yet the explanation for Newcastle's heartbreak lay well before the final frantic minutes. Their early lead had concealed a problem that became increasingly difficult to escape: they were spending too much of the decider defending.

The Knights had the moments. The Roosters kept making them work.

Francis Manuleleua's opening try showed the value of Newcastle's willingness to attack, with Fletcher Sharpe finding his backrower on a strong line. Ponga then supplied the kind of individual intervention capable of defining a Grand Final.

His long range try was particularly extraordinary because of the work that preceded it. The Knights captain was repeatedly involved, covering threats behind his defensive line while remaining central to Newcastle's attack.

But even Ponga could not keep turning survival into points.

At halftime, Newcastle led 12-6 despite making 35 more tackles. Sydney had enjoyed 57% of possession and completed 21 of 23 sets. That disparity mattered more than the Knights' advantage suggested.

Every defensive stand bought Newcastle another chance. Too few of those chances bought their defenders a rest.

The Roosters' territorial pressure meant the Knights repeatedly had to begin again from deep inside their own half. Defusing a kick or stopping a raid was only the first part of the task; finding enough ground to change the next possession was just as important.

Sydney's work through the middle made that difficult. As the match wore on, Newcastle's attempts to shift the ball carried an increasing risk: an error would surrender possession before they had escaped trouble.

This was the tension at the heart of the contest. The Knights needed the ball to relieve the pressure, but the pressure was making it harder to use the ball effectively.

Billy Smith's second half try drew Sydney level. Mark Nawaqanitawase, whose improvised finish had brought the Roosters back into the match before halftime, later completed his double.

Newcastle's resistance had kept the contest alive. Sydney's persistence had changed who controlled it.

Then came Cherry-Evans' field goal.

The veteran's strike pushed the margin beyond a converted try, a decision whose value became clear when Greg Marzhew's late score brought Newcastle back within one point.

For all the attacking talent around him, this was the contribution the Roosters had recruited Cherry-Evans to provide - recognising what the game required and delivering it.

At 37, in his final NRL appearance before joining Hull FC, he finished with a second premiership, 15 years after his first with Manly.

Ahead of the decider, Cherry-Evans had explained how experience had changed his approach.

"I'm obviously more mature, so I have a better understanding of what the team needs," he told the media.

His farewell also gave the result an extra layer of significance. Sandon Smith had left the Roosters following Cherry-Evans' arrival, finding an opportunity in Newcastle that developed into a central role in their premiership push.

The Knights' season had demonstrated how much a fresh opportunity could unlock. Smith, Sharpe and Ponga gave Newcastle a combination capable of troubling opponents in different ways, even after Dylan Brown's ACL injury forced another adjustment.

That progress will matter once the immediate disappointment fades.

Justin Holbrook's side reached the decider through sudden-death victories over South Sydney, the Warriors and Penrith. Their run demanded belief as well as execution, and neither disappeared when the Grand Final began to turn against them.

Their late response ensured Sydney had to finish the job.

But Newcastle could not quite turn that refusal to surrender into one final escape.

For the Roosters, experience helped deliver the ending they wanted. For the Knights, the cruelty was in getting close enough to see theirs.

A season that restored Newcastle's belief ended with a premiership one point beyond reach.
